source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Two models have equal parameter counts but different maximum context lengths measured in tokens. Which conclusion follows from those facts?

options.text: They have different context limits with equal learned parameter counts.
options.feedback: Context capacity and learned parameter count describe different resources. These facts establish a capacity difference, not a universal quality ranking.

options.text: The larger context limit indicates a larger learned parameter set.
options.feedback: The stated parameter counts are equal. A longer context window does not by itself establish a larger parameter set.

options.text: The larger context limit establishes faster completion on comparable tasks.
options.feedback: The facts concern capacity, not latency. Processing more text can require additional work, and speed needs separate evidence.

options.text: The larger context limit establishes better answers on comparable tasks.
options.feedback: A capacity advantage does not guarantee that relevant evidence will be used correctly. Task performance needs to be assessed directly.
